Every module is tested against every set: module 1 holds all 3 X genes and module 0 all 3 Y genes, each a 2.0-fold enrichment with Bonferroni-adjusted p-value 0.29 over the four tests, while the other two pairs have fold 0 and p 1." width="100%"} For each community and each distinct value of the given attribute, tests whether that community is enriched for that value, with multiple-testing correction applied across all tests. This is the usual follow-up to community detection: after `cmty_louvain()` or a similar method has split the network into modules, you want to know what each module "is about" (which pathway, department, topic, or category it is concentrated in). Each (community, value) pair is tested with the one-sided hypergeometric test from `subgraph_enrichment()`, using the whole graph as the background. Because many tests are run at once, some small raw p-values will appear by chance; the `"p_adjusted"` values correct for this and are the ones to use when deciding significance. Nodes that are absent from `communities=` are not tested as part of any community, but they still count toward the graph-wide background (`N` and `K`). Nodes with no value for `attribute=` count toward community and graph sizes but never as hits. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [communities]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [dict[int, int]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping node IDs to community IDs (as returned by `cmty_louvain(return_dict=True)` etc.). Any hashable community IDs work, and they become the top-level keys of the result. [attribute]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Name of the categorical node attribute to test (e.g., `"pathway"` or `"department"`). Every distinct value of the attribute is tested in every community, so the total number of tests is the number of communities times the number of distinct values. [correction]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["bonferroni"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Multiple-testing correction method, applied across all tests together. `"bonferroni"` (default) multiplies each p-value by the number of tests (capped at `1`); it is conservative and controls the chance of any false positive. `"fdr"` applies the Benjamini-Hochberg procedure, which controls the expected proportion of false discoveries and is less strict, so it is usually preferred when many communities or values are tested. Any other value raises a `ValueError`. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [dict[int, dict]]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Dictionary mapping community IDs to enrichment results. Each result is a dict mapping attribute values to enrichment dicts (same structure as `subgraph_enrichment()`: `"value"`, `"k"`, `"K"`, `"n"`, `"N"`, `"p_value"`, `"fold_enrichment"`), with an additional `"p_adjusted"` key holding the corrected p-value. ::: ## Raises {.doc-raises} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ValueError]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : If `correction=` is not `"bonferroni"` or `"fdr"`. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Eight genes form two modules joined by the edge "G4"-"G5". Genes "G1" to "G3" belong to gene set "X" and "G6" to "G8" to set "Y". Passing the module membership explicitly, each module is two-fold enriched for its own gene set. The raw p-value is `0.071`, and after Bonferroni correction over the four tests (2 modules x 2 sets) it becomes `0.286`: ::: {#547cbd73 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ec.Graph() graph.add_nodes([f"G{i}" for i in range(1, 9)]) graph.add_edges([ ("G1", "G2"), ("G2", "G3"), ("G3", "G1"), ("G1", "G4"), ("G2", "G4"), ("G4", "G5"), ("G5", "G6"), ("G6", "G7"), ("G7", "G8"), ("G8", "G5"), ("G5", "G7"), ("G6", "G8"), ]) gene_sets = {"G1": "X", "G2": "X", "G3": "X", "G6": "Y", "G7": "Y", "G8": "Y"} graph.set_node_attrs( "gene_set", {graph.get_id_from_label(g): s for g, s in gene_sets.items()} ) modules = { graph.get_id_from_label(f"G{i}"): ("left" if i <= 4 else "right") for i in range(1, 9) } results = graph.module_annotation_enrichment(modules, "gene_set") { (module, value): (r["k"], r["fold_enrichment"], round(r["p_value"], 3), round(r["p_adjusted"], 3)) for module, by_value in results.items() for value, r in by_value.items() } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` {('left', 'X'): (3, 2.0, 0.071, 0.286), ('left', 'Y'): (0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0), ('right', 'X'): (0, 0.0, 1.0, 1.0), ('right', 'Y'): (3, 2.0, 0.071, 0.286)} ``` ::: ::: The Benjamini-Hochberg correction (`correction="fdr"`) is less strict, so the same two enrichments get a smaller adjusted p-value of about `0.143`: ::: {#99a60bc6 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} results = graph.module_annotation_enrichment(modules, "gene_set", correction="fdr") round(results["left"]["X"]["p_adjusted"], 3), round(results["right"]["Y"]["p_adjusted"], 3) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` (0.143, 0.143) ``` ::: ::: In practice the communities usually come straight from a community-detection method. Here Louvain recovers the same two modules, and each is enriched for one gene set: ::: {#57240f29 .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} communities = graph.cmty_louvain(return_dict=True) results = graph.module_annotation_enrichment(communities, "gene_set") { cmty: max(by_value, key=lambda v: by_value[v]["fold_enrichment"]) for cmty, by_value in results.items() } ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` {1: 'Y', 0: 'X'} ``` ::: :::
